column1: # NAMED CONSTRAINT ALIASES -- the `type()`-marked definitions block.
# The algebra has no int8/uint16/port keyword and does not need one: a
# constraint is a value, so a name for one is a field, and `type()`
# keeps the definitions out of the output while they still unify.
# docs/design/AONTUCONSTRAINTS.0.md wanted sized-integer sugar built
# into the language (its "free win" once bounds exist); these rows are
# why that was declined -- the idiom is already expressible, and unlike
# a keyword it composes and is not a closed list.
# Normative: docs/reference-language.md "Named constraint aliases";
# task form in docs/how-to.md "Name a reusable constraint". Both are
# executed by ts/test/docs.test.ts, so these rows and those pages
# cannot drift apart silently.
# Every expectation was obtained by running BOTH engines and diffing
# full output, per the parity probe. Columns: name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
alias-uint8-accepts
alias-uint8-rejects-above
# The refusal lands at the field that holds the value, not at the
# definition -- an agent reading `path` is sent where the fix goes.
alias-uint8-rejects-path
# LEAD WITH THE KIND. This is the trap the idiom invites and the reason
# every alias in the documentation starts with `integer`: bounds alone
# bound a NUMBER, so a float in range satisfies them. Both rows are
# correct behaviour; they are here as a pair so the difference is a
# pinned contract rather than a surprise.
alias-kind-named-rejects-float
alias-kind-omitted-admits-float
# `type` is not a reserved word -- the mark does the work, not the name.
alias-key-name-not-reserved
# Aliases are ordinary values, so they compose both ways: one defined
# in terms of another, and one met with a further constraint at the
# point of use.
alias-of-alias
alias-narrowed-at-use
# NOT PINNED HERE, deliberately: a composed alias that is VIOLATED. Both
# ports refuse, with the same code and the same path, but they name
# different residuals -- TypeScript the merged `integer&min(0)&max(15)`,
# Go only the local `max(15)`, at different sites. A row must pass in
# both. use-cases/BUGS.md 48.
